s1.p1: Recursion is a process in which a function calls itself, either directly or indirectly
s1.p2: In functional programming, a recursive function is a ‘purer’ alternative to a loop
s1.p3: ![ico-20 warn] Every recursive function must have a condition to terminate the recursion
s1.p4: Otherwise, calling the function will result in an infinite loop
s1.p5: **Tail recursion** is when the last statement executed by a recursive function is the **_return_** statement, which calls the function itself
s1.p6: The simplest (classic) example of recursion is calculating a factorial
s1.p7: To get rid of the optional parameter, we use closure:
s1.p8: In JavaScript, every function call adds a call frame to the stack
s1.p9: When the call completes, the frame is removed from the stack
s1.p10: However, a recursive function does not terminate immediately
s1.p11: It will return a recursive call to itself
s1.p12: If tail recursion is deep enough, this can lead to a stack overflow and the generation of an exception ![ico-20 err] **⟦f0⟧**
s1.p13: ^^The **⟦f0⟧** exception occurs when the depth of recursion exceeds 10,000^^
